summary: Charles Kirkconnell International Airport (CYB) is the primary gateway to Cayman Brac and Little Cayman, two of the three Cayman Islands. Named after Captain Charles Kirkconnell, a local aviation pioneer and community leader, the airport serves the quiet Sister Islands with a single runway. It provides essential connectivity for residents and visitors heading to this remote and pristine region known for world-class diving and dramatic limestone bluffs.
faqs:
Q: Which islands does Charles Kirkconnell International Airport serve?
A: The airport serves Cayman Brac and Little Cayman, known collectively as the Sister Islands of the Cayman Islands archipelago.

Q: How long is the runway at CYB?
A: The airport features a single asphalt runway approximately 6,700 feet long, capable of handling regional jets including Boeing 737s and 757s.

Q: Are there flights to Grand Cayman from this airport?
A: Yes, short inter-island flights connect CYB to Owen Roberts International Airport in Grand Cayman, as well as to Miami and other regional destinations.

Q: What facilities are available at the terminal?
A: The terminal offers standard amenities including a small lounge, restrooms, car rental counters, and basic concessions, reflecting the airport's medium-sized, low-traffic profile.
transport_tips: The airport is located just minutes from West End village, making ground transportation quick and straightforward. Rental cars, taxis, and pre-arranged hotel shuttles are the main ways to reach accommodations on Cayman Brac. Since the island is only about 12 miles long, no destination is more than a 30-minute drive from the terminal.
local_tip: Bring reef-safe sunscreen and a light jacket for the windward side of the island—the airport sits near the coast and breezes can pick up quickly, especially on flights to and from Miami.
